page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. The page opens mid-sentence and the column ends with a catchword-free signature mark below the text.

main_text.p: plures civitates dedicaverunt. Nam & ad hæc tempora Scythæ Armeni urbes habent Olybama & Arsa Ratha, & ejusdemodi, Berosus. Incolæ in Armenia Saga ipsum Noa, omnium Deorum patrem, vocant: & primum dixerunt Ogygisan Sagam, id est, illustrem sacrorum pontificem Noam Dysir. (M. Porcius Cato etiam Sagos primos Thuscos, interpretatur pontifices & sacros expiatores.) Thyseam vero (alii Tideam, nimirum ejus uxorem) Aretiam dixerunt, id est, Terram, & Estam, id est, Ignem, (אש[?] esch enim ignis Hebræis) post mortem cognominaverunt: quia ipsa regina sacrorum fuerat, & puellas docuerat Noa cogno-minatus janum. sempiternum ignem sacrorum servare. Vino etiam invento Noa cognominatus est janus; quod Aramæis sonat vitifer, & vinifer. (יין jain enim Hebræis vinum est.) Plinius scribit Scythas, vocatos esse Sacas a Persis, & lingua Persica Aramæos.

Exsiccata post diluvium humo, Noa de monte Armeniæ Gordyæo descendit in subjacentem planiciem plenam cadaverum, quam usque ad hanc ætatem appellant Myry Adam, id est, evisceratorum hominum. Filium Cham infamia & impudentia insignem Chemesenua cognominavit, id est, Cham infamem & impudicum, incubum, propagatorem. Est enim Esen apud Scythas Aramæos in-

page.notes: The first Hebrew word in the parenthesis after "Ignem," is only partly legible and is read as אש with a doubt marker. The Hebrew word "יין" after "vinifer" is read with some uncertainty. The first letters of "Est enim Esen" at the end of the page are faint, and the page breaks off at "in-" so the sentence continues on the next page. The margin note is set in three short lines (cogno- / minatus / janum.) and is given here as one note. The running head and page number are clear. The signature "B 4" is printed at the foot, with the "4" slightly unclear.
